vocabulary.definition: without an end; having or seeming to have no end
vocabulary.example: The possibilities for exploration in space seem to be endless.

vocabulary.definition: existing at or from the beginning of time; primeval
vocabulary.example: The primordial soup theory suggests that life on Earth began from simple organic compounds.

vocabulary.definition: the process of growth or increase, typically by the gradual accumulation of additional layers or matter
vocabulary.example: The formation of planets from dust and gas involves the process of accretion.

vocabulary.definition: a massive and extremely remote celestial object, emitting exceptionally large amounts of energy
vocabulary.example: Quasars are some of the most luminous objects in the universe.

vocabulary.definition: a point at which a function takes an infinite value, especially in space-time when matter is infinitely dense, as at the center of a black hole
vocabulary.example: The concept of a singularity at the center of a black hole challenges our understanding of physics.

vocabulary.definition: having an excessive preoccupation with something; constantly worrying or thinking about something
vocabulary.example: Her obsessive need for perfection made her spend hours refining her work.
